introSection.heading: Choosing the Right Princess Ship
introSection.p1: Choosing the right Princess Cruises ship can shape your entire holiday. While every ship offers the line’s signature service, dining, entertainment and MedallionClass technology, the fleet ranges from the expansive Sphere Class to smaller vessels designed for itineraries where access and destination time matter as much as onboard facilities.
introSection.p2: The best Princess ship for you depends on how you like to travel. Some guests want the newest venues and a wide choice of restaurants. Others prefer a more traditional ship, a quieter atmosphere or a vessel suited to a particular itinerary, such as the Panama Canal or an extended voyage.
introSection.p3: This guide compares the Princess Cruises fleet, highlights the differences between its ships and explains how to narrow your choice.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer: Which Princess Ship Is Best for You?
quickAnswer.subtitle: Starting points based on your personal travel priorities and holiday preferences

priorities.title: Newest Onboard Experience
priorities.description: Star Princess (2025) or Sun Princess (2024). Next-generation resort ships featuring contemporary architectural design, The Dome entertainment space, and the exclusive Sanctuary Collection suites and private dining.

priorities.title: Large Ship with Broadest Venues
priorities.description: Discovery Princess, Enchanted Princess, or Sky Princess. Modern flagships offering a high proportion of balcony accommodation, expanded multi-story Piazza hubs, and Sky Suites featuring the largest continuous balconies at sea.

priorities.title: Modern Facilities & Familiar Layout
priorities.description: Royal Princess, Regal Princess, or Majestic Princess. Well-established modern large ships delivering signature amenities like the SeaWalk glass walkway, Lotus Spa, and diverse specialty dining.

priorities.title: Smaller-Ship Intimacy & Destination Time
priorities.description: Coral Princess or Island Princess (approximately 2,000–2,200 guests). Intimate proportions with open wraparound decks, fewer crowds, and superior access to destination-focused ports.

priorities.title: Full-Transit Panama Canal Itineraries
priorities.description: Coral Princess or Island Princess. Specifically engineered to navigate the historic locks of the Panama Canal on complete ocean-to-ocean transit routes that larger megaships cannot sail.

priorities.title: Classic Traditional Princess Cruising
priorities.description: Grand Princess, Ruby Princess, Emerald Princess, or Crown Princess. Cherished traditional ocean-liner feel with classic teak promenade decks, Movies Under the Stars, and exceptional value.

priorities.title: Asia & Exotic Seasonal Sailings
priorities.description: Diamond Princess and Sapphire Princess. Specially appointed with authentic Izumi Japanese open-air baths and regionally tailored culinary programmes deployed across Asia and the Pacific.

fleetClasses.title: Understanding the Princess Cruises Fleet
fleetClasses.subtitle: An in-depth guide to the four distinctive ship classes across the 17-vessel fleet

classes.name: Sphere Class: Sun Princess & Star Princess
classes.description: The Sphere Class represents the newest generation of Princess ships. Sun Princess entered service in 2024, followed by Star Princess in 2025. Both accommodate approximately 4,300 guests at double occupancy and are the largest vessels in the fleet. Their design introduces a contemporary resort environment with distinctive public spaces, The Dome entertainment arena, and the private Sanctuary Collection experience.
classes.bestFor: Travellers who value cutting-edge design, broad dining variety, and vibrant resort-style cruising. Mediterranean & Caribbean flagships.

classes.name: Royal Class: Discovery, Enchanted, Sky, Majestic, Regal & Royal Princess
classes.description: The six Royal Class vessels combine substantial onboard facilities with a beloved, familiar Princess layout. They feature multi-deck Italian Piazza atriums, cantilevered SeaWalk glass corridors over the ocean, Princess Live! broadcast lounges, and Sky Suites offering panoramic 270-degree balcony views.
classes.bestFor: Cruisers wanting extensive amenities, world-class entertainment, multiple dining venues, and a wide selection of balcony stateroom categories.

classes.name: Grand Class & Mid-Sized Princess Ships
classes.description: Encompassing Caribbean, Crown, Emerald, Grand, Ruby, Diamond, and Sapphire Princess, these mid-sized vessels provide a traditional ocean cruise experience. They feature expansive teak promenade decks, classic nautical lounges, Sabatini's Italian Trattoria, and Crown Grill steakhouses with highly competitive cruise fares.
classes.bestFor: Guests who appreciate classic maritime layouts, quieter atmospheres, relaxed sea days, and destination-rich global itineraries.

classes.name: Coral Class: Coral Princess & Island Princess
classes.description: Coral Princess and Island Princess are among the most intimate ships in the fleet. Their specialized Panamax dimensions allow them to operate historic full-transit Panama Canal voyages, remote world cruise segments, and long exotic itineraries where larger ships cannot navigate.
classes.bestFor: Travellers who prioritize port access, longer itineraries, Panama Canal transits, and an intimate ship atmosphere with fewer fellow passengers.

travellerProfiles.title: Which Princess Ship Is Best for Different Types of Travellers?
travellerProfiles.subtitle: Matching specific travel styles, travel companions, and itinerary preferences to the right ship

features.title: For First-Time Princess Cruisers
features.description: Start by comparing Sun Princess, Star Princess, or modern Royal Class vessels (Discovery, Enchanted, Sky). They showcase the brand's full range of specialty dining, Broadway-style entertainment, vibrant Piazza atriums, and seamless MedallionClass technology.

features.title: For Families with Children & Teens
features.description: Sphere Class and Royal Class ships offer the broadest variety: dedicated Camp Discovery youth centers (ages 3–17), multi-pool complexes, outdoor sports courts, and connecting staterooms for family convenience.

features.title: For Couples & Romantic Getaways
features.description: Couples seeking contemporary luxury will love the Sanctuary Collection aboard Sun and Star Princess. For a more intimate, classic cruise atmosphere, the quieter lounges and ocean-view dining of Coral or Grand Class vessels provide romantic tranquility.

features.title: For Longer Voyages & World Cruises
features.description: Extended itineraries demand comfortable staterooms, self-service laundromats, diverse sea-day enrichment lectures, and uncrowded public lounges. Coral Princess and Island Princess excel on 20+ night grand voyages.

features.title: For Alaska & Scenic Cruising
features.description: Select based on itinerary and glacier-viewing access first (Glacier Bay National Park, College Fjord). Royal Class ships feature cantilevered SeaWalks, while Grand and Coral Class vessels offer open wraparound promenade decks ideal for wildlife spotting.

features.title: For Panama Canal Transits
features.description: Coral Princess and Island Princess are the premier choices for ocean-to-ocean Panama Canal voyages, as their classic Panamax proportions permit passage through the original historic locks.

features.title: For Travellers Who Prefer Newest Ships
features.description: Sun Princess and Star Princess offer the latest Sphere Class innovations, upgraded staterooms with sofa beds, sustainable LNG propulsion, and spectacular multi-level venues like The Dome.

checklist.title: What to Check Before Choosing Your Princess Ship
checklist.subtitle: An eight-point evaluation checklist before confirming your reservation

steps.title: 1. Itinerary & Port Time
steps.description: Does the ship visit the destinations you prioritize, and does it spend sufficient daylight hours in key ports?

steps.title: 2. Ship Size & Vibe
steps.description: Decide whether you prefer a 4,300-guest resort ship with endless activities or a 2,000-guest intimate vessel with a calmer pace.

steps.title: 3. Dining Preferences
steps.description: Check if your favorite specialty venues (Crown Grill, Sabatini's, The Catch by Rudi, Alfredo's) are available on that specific ship.

steps.title: 4. Stateroom Categories
steps.description: Review deck plans for square footage, balcony dimensions, connecting doors, and whether Sanctuary or Reserve Collection is offered.

steps.title: 5. Travel Dates & Season
steps.description: Ensure the sailing dates align with your vacation schedule and regional seasonal weather patterns.

steps.title: 6. Refurbishment History
steps.description: For older Grand and Coral Class vessels, check recent dry-dock upgrades, refreshed carpets, and updated venue configurations.

steps.title: 7. Package Inclusions
steps.description: Factor in Princess Plus ($70–$75/day) or Premier ($105–$110/day) costs to calculate your realistic total holiday budget.

steps.title: 8. Accessibility & Mobility
steps.description: Verify wheelchair-accessible staterooms, pool lifts, and accessible tenders if your itinerary includes tender ports.

advisor.name: Angela Hughes
advisor.title: CEO of Trips & Ships Luxury Travel
advisor.bio: With more than 40 years of luxury travel-industry experience and having explored over 121 countries across all seven continents, Angela Hughes provides expert guidance on navigating Princess Cruises ship selection, stateroom categories, and worldwide itineraries.
advisor.quote: Choosing the right Princess ship isn't simply about picking the newest vessel. For an Alaska voyage or a Panama Canal transit, a mid-sized ship like Coral or Sapphire can offer a far richer destination experience than a 4,300-guest megaship.

faqs.question: How many ships does Princess Cruises have?
faqs.answer: Princess Cruises currently operates a fleet of 17 ships, ranging from the newer Sphere Class vessels to smaller ships such as Coral Princess and Island Princess.

faqs.question: What is the newest Princess Cruises ship?
faqs.answer: Star Princess, which entered service in 2025, is the newest ship in the Princess fleet as of November 2026, following her sister ship Sun Princess (2024).

faqs.question: What is the largest Princess Cruises ship?
faqs.answer: Sun Princess and Star Princess are the largest ships in the fleet by passenger capacity and gross tonnage, each accommodating approximately 4,300 guests at double occupancy.

faqs.question: Which Princess ship is the smallest?
faqs.answer: Coral Princess is the smallest ship in the current fleet by passenger capacity, accommodating approximately 2,000 guests at double occupancy.

faqs.question: Which Princess ship is best for the Panama Canal?
faqs.answer: Coral Princess and Island Princess are strong options to compare for full-transit Panama Canal itineraries because their smaller dimensions allow them to operate routes through the historic locks that larger ships cannot. Confirm the transit type on the specific sailing.

faqs.question: Which Princess ship is best for families?
faqs.answer: There is no single best ship for every family. Compare the youth facilities (Camp Discovery), pool areas, entertainment, family stateroom options, and itinerary on the exact ship. Larger Sphere and Royal Class ships generally offer a wider range of public spaces and activities.

faqs.question: Are older Princess ships still worth booking?
faqs.answer: Yes. An older ship can be a good choice when its facilities, cabin options, itinerary, and fare suit your needs. Older ships often feature classic wraparound promenade decks and visit destination-rich ports. Review current deck plans and refurbishment details before booking.

faqs.question: Are all Princess ships the same?
faqs.answer: No. All ships share the Princess brand experience and MedallionClass technology, but their size, layouts, dining venues, public spaces, and itineraries vary considerably across the four ship classes.

faqs.question: Do all Princess ships offer the Sanctuary Collection?
faqs.answer: No. The Sanctuary Collection is exclusively associated with Sun Princess and Star Princess. Reserve Collection accommodations and benefits are available on qualifying mini-suites and staterooms on other eligible ships, subject to current booking terms.

faqs.question: How do I choose between Sun Princess and Star Princess?
faqs.answer: Compare the itinerary, departure port, travel dates, stateroom availability, fare, and onboard venue details. As sister ships, they share the Sphere Class design, so practical differences in the sailing itinerary may be the deciding factor.
